narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 22% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the threshold set by the school, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help ensure your success.

The prediction was influenced most strongly by three aspects of your profile. First, your record shows that you have not failed any classes in the past, which is a positive sign and actually reduced your risk compared to others—most students in your situation also have no prior failures, and this worked in your favor. Second, you are currently taking extra paid classes within your course subject. While only a small percentage of students do this, the model found that, for students like you, participating in these paid classes was linked to a higher chance of struggling in the final year. This may be because students who seek out extra paid help are already finding the material challenging. Third, your strong desire to pursue higher education also helped lower your risk, as every student in your group shares this goal, and it is generally associated with better outcomes.

Although some factors worked in your favor, the combination of needing extra paid support and other elements in your profile led the model to recommend remedial courses. Taking these courses is an opportunity to strengthen your understanding and improve your chances of passing. It’s important to engage fully with the support offered and to reach out for help whenever you need it.
